persona.circumstances: Aoife is a 34-year-old living in Belfast, Northern Ireland, where she has held a short-term medical driving licence since being diagnosed with epilepsy in her mid-twenties. She completed her CBT motorcycle training at 19 before switching primarily to car driving after her diagnosis meant she needed regular medical review of her licence. Her current short-term licence is due to expire soon, and her neurologist has confirmed she remains fit to drive, so she now needs to go through the renewal process again, which she has done a couple of times before. Because she lives in Northern Ireland rather than Great Britain, she knows the DVA (not DVLA) handles her licence, and she's navigating the online guidance to make sure she ends up on the right page for her specific situation.

persona.likely_friction: Much of the official guidance defaults to GB/DVLA processes, so she may struggle to quickly find the NI/DVA-specific equivalent forms and contact points, causing frustration and repeated backtracking through menus designed around England, Scotland and Wales residents.

persona.name: Craig Bellamy
persona.circumstances: Craig is 30 and passed his full car test back when he was 19, well before February 2001, so under the old rules his car licence already carries motorcycle/moped entitlement categories from that era.
